I need to find a good strength training routine for a complete weakling.

This winter I fell very ill, could barely eat for a month, and lost around 20% of my body weight. Because of that, I find I can't do a single proper pushup and curls with an empty barbell is very tiring.

I've never been this weak before and have no idea how to start training. So far I'm just trying knee pushups and working out with a barbell. I have no idea if this is the best way to start though.

I'm sure someone on here has actual advice but knee pushups, barbell curls etc... will all do the job. Just be consistent and you'll see progress, it's going to suck for a while and you are probably going to hate being so weak but as long as you keep at it you'll get there.

You're probably right. I just hoped there was a faster way to get started. I don't think there are shortcuts at any level though.

Any suggestions for working the core? My back seems to like the free weight curls and barbell squats, but abs and obliques could use some love too.

You're right about hating being this weak too. I keep inadvertantly hurting myself lifting and moving everyday objects too, so I'm done ignoring the problem and hoping it will return naturally.

I don't know if your arms are strong enough for planks but that's a pretty simple and effective ab workout. Again I wish I was more help but I just started working out a few months ago from being a scrawny nerd so my experience is limited.

If you are recovering from serious illness it may be worth consulting a physiotherapist out hopefully one can chime in here.

I had a shoulder injury and lost most strength in it the recovery was using resistance bands of various levels to slowly build up strength before returning to the normal pushups etc. I was doing before hand.

Edit: just adding a link to the exercises I was given you May be able too look around the site for Some things relevant too yourself http://www.physioadvisor.com.au/8122150/shoulder-strengthening-exercises-shoulder-rehabi.htm

Any reasonable bodyweight fitness progression will help. Pushups as an example: start with wall pushups, then high angle incline pushups, mid angle, low angle, and eventually you'll be back to real pushups.

http://1.bp.blogspot.com/-Bymi7PIcwbw/Ut9zdrIR8AI/AAAAAAAAB9w/B7sa2I0Y1Pc/s1600/POSTER+FINAL-page-001.jpg That's a body weight fitness program that may be able to help. It starts out light and slowly ramps up, and it might be best to start out doing only body weight exercises. A good place to go after that may be to start doing lifts with dumbbells like dumbbell bench press and the such because you can start off very light with those. Best of luck! I'm happy to try and help if you have any questions!
